column17: ADDED 2026-07-31 (FFR-PA re-query) as the MISO analogue of PJM's Eddystone rows. The 2026-07-05 pass held Campbell out entirely, reasoning 'no binding retirement date currently exists — the opposite of confirmed'. That is the definition of a SUPERSEDED row, not of an absent one: the binding date does exist (MPSC U-21090, 2025-05-31) and is currently overridden by a rolling DOE §202(c) order chain, exactly the Eddystone pattern the schema's superseded flag was designed around. Registering it superseded=true (a) preserves the audit trail the plan §2.2 requires for counter-instruments, (b) keeps the loader ignoring it so the economic screen governs — no change to any exit, and (c) makes plant 1710 fully-superseded, so load_announced_reversal_plants suppresses the stale EIA-860 planned_retirement_year=2026 for a plant that is demonstrably still running under federal compulsion. Campbell is coal, so under the default forecast_fossil_retirement_economic=True the announced channel is a no-op for it either way: this row changes no default-config result. Current order 202-26-22 expires 2026-08-16 — re-query then, alongside Eddystone's 2026-08-22.
